canonical_question: Why does the 'in situ TEM annealing' result in such minimal grain growth (24.5 nm to 26.3 nm) compared to the significant changes seen under irradiation?

question_variants.question: Why does the 'in situ TEM annealing' result in such minimal grain growth (24.5 nm to 26.3 nm) compared to the significant changes seen under irradiation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The in situ TEM annealing at 1173 K resulted in minimal grain growth (24.5 nm to 26.3 nm). The evidence provides the numerical data for the grain size change but does not explicitly explain the mechanism for why this growth is so minimal compared to irradiation effects.

answers.answer: The average grain size increased from 24.5 ± 1.3 nm (as-deposited) to 26.3 ± 1.1 nm after annealing to 1173 K for ~30 mins. The text notes the stability but does not provide the specific reason for the minimal growth compared to irradiation.
answers.mechanism: High thermal stability inferred from minimal growth.
answers.boundary_limitation: Mechanism for minimal growth relative to irradiation is not detailed.
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time
